dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SURVEY SHIP — THE LATTICE

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEY CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Has someone left a camera feed on repeat?

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEY OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: It's optical and instrument return. Different systems. Same feature.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Then verify our position independently.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: I already did. Three times.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Do it again while I find someone clever enough to tell us why three times wasn't sufficient.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: The corridor is still inside the safe envelope.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Safe according to the model that's just shown us two copies of the same star. Reduce speed. Keep recording everything.

panelPlan: SURVEY SHIP — THE LATTICE. On a route that has behaved predictably for months, a survey crew checks field transit timing. Every verified reference is healthy..
The reflected star shifts with the ship's attitude change, but not by the amount the model predicts.
They do not call it a ghost or a portent. They call home.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: VEIL MARKET

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: The last buyer wanted a refund because a star was in the wrong place. I explained that I have never guaranteed the position of stars.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You're guaranteeing safe windows. If the timing has changed, the guarantee is worth less than the paper.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: The timing hasn't changed.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: That's what frightens me. Every clock agrees, and something is still wrong.

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: The field isn't opening another corridor. The returns are being phase-repeated through the measured volume. That's a description, not a cause.

dialogueInline.speaker: SELENE
dialogueInline.text: Older logs contain accounts of apparent doubled vessels near lost anchors.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: And how many of those logs include a surviving sensor calibration?

dialogueInline.speaker: SELENE
dialogueInline.text: Very few.

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: Then they're interesting, not confirmatory.

panelPlan: VEIL MARKET. Jex has already discovered that the anomaly has reduced the value of his old route windows. Naomi brings him unedited survey data.
At Thunderbreak, Jia Morgan measures the deviation against Academy reciprocal-field models. Selene has brought historical survey records, but not explanations.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: You can work with that distinction?

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: I can work with uncertainty. It's commanders who insist on making it uncomfortable.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Commodore, this is not reinstatement to Thunderbreak. Deka remains responsible for the vessel. You coordinate the Fleet task group for the corridor emergency.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Thank you for explaining who owns the chair. We've had a surprisingly spirited argument about it.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: We haven't had an argument.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Then you've been losing one without noticing.

panelPlan: Dominion appears long enough to confirm Venn's limited task-group appointment. The tribunal has not been overturned. Deka's command remains in force.
Jia resumes the measurements before the officers can enjoy themselves.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: TAL CORVUS / ASHFANG — SURVEY DISCUSSION

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: If something's making copies of ships, I want to know what happens when I shoot one.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: We've no data that suggests it has a surface or that a projectile can hit it.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: We could acquire some.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: By firing through a civilian corridor?

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: I said I wanted to know. I didn't say I wanted to do it here.

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: Some of the footage may be an instrumentation error.

dialogueInline.speaker: FEAR MASK
dialogueInline.text: The people won't see the instrument. They'll see a ship where no ship should be.

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: You want them to think it means the passage is closed?

dialogueInline.speaker: FEAR MASK
dialogueInline.text: I want them to ask our permission before they travel.

panelPlan: Tal Corvus. Tess keeps civilians away from the unexplained seep and anomalous viewing area before discussing theories. On Ashfang, Billie examines the same.
In the Arena Vault, Fear distributes the most disturbing images as proof the corridors have become uncontrollable.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: CALM CORRIDOR — SUNLASH / GRAVEFIRE

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND
dialogueInline.text: Naomi, there's another Gravefire on our starboard feed.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Which one's answering the real transponder?

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND
dialogueInline.text: One. The other is agreeing with it before the answer arrives.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: That's inconvenient. Tess, what are you seeing?

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: A beautifully repaired version of my ship. I'm tempted to ask it to lend me a radiator.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Don't go toward it.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I'd have to leave the civilians to do that. I don't think even I like my reflection enough.

panelPlan: Sunlash leads a civilian convoy toward the Calm Corridor. Gravefire holds the rear. The first reflected vessel appears beside Tess's ship, matching its damage.
An inexperienced pilot begins turning toward the apparent path of an escort. Tess calmly orders him back to the surveyed lane. The reflection looks real and.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: THUNDERBREAK

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: Every time the formation makes the same correction, the delayed returns grow more coherent. If they are phase-locking, then varying the inputs should make the pattern collapse.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Should?

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: Yes. I'd prefer to use a different word, but it would be dishonest.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: We can test it with the escorts before we put the freighters through.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: We don't have an empty corridor for an elegant experiment. I can stagger the actual formation. Different speeds, different attitudes, no one copying the same turn.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: We stop synchronized firing as well. No ship fires merely because another has fired.

dialogueInline.speaker: JIA
dialogueInline.text: I don't know that the field responds to weapons specifically. It may respond to any coherent input.

panelPlan: THUNDERBREAK. Jia compares synchronized ship inputs against the growth of the echoes.
directionInline: Use released Rex Fleet references for appearance, faction and ship design. Preserve exact dialogue, action and speaker order.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Then we stop making coherent ones. That's unusually easy to explain to this crew.

dialogueInline.speaker: FREIGHTER PILOT
dialogueInline.text: We're losing the escort pattern!

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: On purpose. You're not abandoned. You're being asked to fly your own ship for the next two minutes.

dialogueInline.speaker: FREIGHTER PILOT
dialogueInline.text: I thought we hired escorts to avoid that.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You hired us to bring you home. Not to make the ride pretty.

panelPlan: The convoy breaks formation deliberately. Naomi gives one freighter a wide safe turn, another a shallow reduction. Tess keeps the trailing craft from trying to.
Echoes lose their crisp synchronization. The physical solution is untidy and measurable. No one claims to know why the effect exists.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: VEIL MARKET

dialogueInline.speaker: BUYER
dialogueInline.text: I don't need a scientific explanation. I need the safest forecast you can sell me.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I can tell you where the observations were made and how uncertain they are. I cannot sell you a number that means something different every time a ship passes it.

dialogueInline.speaker: BUYER
dialogueInline.text: You used to be more helpful.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I used to be more expensive. Those aren't the same thing.

panelPlan: VEIL MARKET. A buyer demands an exclusive warning service for the strange corridor behavior. Jex looks at the contract, then at the unverified claims already.
At the Arena Vault, Fear decides that the independent witnesses are becoming more dangerous than the anomaly itself. Its emissary turns from the corridor.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: CALM CORRIDOR — CIVILIAN ARRIVALS

dialogueInline.speaker: ENGINEER
dialogueInline.text: You can stop staring now. They're through.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I heard you.

dialogueInline.speaker: ENGINEER
dialogueInline.text: You've been standing for fourteen hours.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Then get me a chair, not a lecture.

dialogueInline.speaker: ENGINEER
dialogueInline.text: It tilts.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: So does the ship. I'll feel at home.

panelPlan: The convoy emerges in a crooked order with all the ships intact. Tess waits on Gravefire until the last civilian docking light is confirmed.
The engineer produces a chair that has been pushed into a corner for repairs.
She sits only after the last light steadies. From the outer viewport, the corridor looks ordinary again. Nobody knows if it will remain that way.
